subject: Unexpected July charges — suspected phantom requests from rotated API keys
messages:
From: Anjali Rao <anjali@nebulacorp.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: finance@nebulacorp.com
Date: Tue, 09 Nov 2027 18:22:00 +0000
Subject: Unexpected July charges — noticed large phantom ingest

Hi Sofia,

I'm writing from Nebula's finance team — we just reviewed the July invoice and saw a ~47k token overage (line item: "ingest-requests: bulk"), which doesn't match any of the activity our product team is seeing. We've pulled request_ids from our side and are attaching the sample export (usage_samples_nebula_20271109.csv).

A couple of observations from our engineers:
- The spike aligns to 2027-07-21 02:00–03:00 UTC.
- The requests in question reference an API key that was rotated on 2027-07-20 (je-rot-78).
- We do see a handful of request_ids that look like staging/test traffic but billed under our production org.

We need:
1) A full usage export for the July 20–22 window with request_id, model, token counts, and the originating API key.
2) Evidence that requests were attributed to our account (headers, prefix match, or account_id).
3) A provisional credit while you investigate — we will hold the July payment pending confirmation.

Please let me know next steps and a timeline. We're also trying to understand VAT treatment if a credit is granted (we're EU-based).

Thanks,

Anjali Rao
Head of Finance, Nebula Corp
finance@nebulacorp.com

Attachments: usage_samples_nebula_20271109.csv (CSV, 78 rows)
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Anjali Rao <anjali@nebulacorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 09 Nov 2027 19:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Unexpected July charges — noticed large phantom ingest

Hi Anjali — thanks for flagging this and for the sample export, that was helpful. I've opened an internal investigation and looped in Ben (billing) and Kimberly (account ops).

High level plan and asks from our side:
- We'll produce the requested July 20–22 usage export with request_id, token breakdown, and the API key fingerprint by EOD tomorrow (Nov 10).
- We'll run a cross-check for key reuse and cross-tenant attribution; preliminary look suggests there may have been an edge-case where a rotated key string mapped to a retained staging record in our ingest pipeline.
- We can provisionally apply a credit for the disputed token charge while we finish the forensic audit; Ben can confirm the credit amount and how VAT will be handled.

Next steps:
- Ben: can you confirm provisional credit process and ETA for the credit memo + whether we need a signed DocuSign for accounting?
- Kimberly: please capture the investigation notes (root cause hypotheses, TTL of logs, recommended remediation).

Anjali — we'll aim to have the export and a proposed credit amount (tokens and EUR) by 24 hours. If you need a formal collection hold note for your AR team, tell me how you'd like it worded and we'll deliver it.

Best,

Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Nov 2027 10:17:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Unexpected July charges — provisional credit proposal and evidence

FYI — internal notes and proposed action. Forwarding the thread to billing ops record.

Investigation summary (preliminary):
- Usage export pulled for 2027-07-20 00:00 to 2027-07-22 23:59 UTC.
- 3,842 requests attributed to Nebula's org_id (org-NEB-001) with a combined delta of 48,130 tokens over expected baseline.
- 94% of those requests originate from API key fingerprint 'je-rot-78' (rotated key). Our ingest pipeline kept a short-lived mapping for that key in a cache for 18 hours due to a bug in key-rotation cleanup; during that window, sandbox traffic with identical prefixes was erroneously attributed to the production org.

Proposed remediation and accounting steps:
1) Issue a provisional credit equal to the disputed token cost: 48,130 tokens * €0.00045 = €21.66 (pre-VAT).
2) Apply the credit to the July invoice and issue a credit memo PDF (invoice_NEB-202711-Jul-credit.pdf).
3) VAT handling: Because the original invoice included EU VAT, we'll issue a credit memo that mirrors VAT lines — accounting team to treat it as a negative invoice. Kimberly, pls advise if Nebula prefers a posted credit or a DocuSign-backed memo for reconciliation.
4) Remediation: patch to key-rotation cleanup shipped (PR#4892), and we'll keep a one-week log export available for Nebula's audit.

Attachments referenced for Nebula: usage_export_20270720-22.csv (redacted PII), invoice_NEB-202711-Jul.pdf

Action items:
- Sofia: confirm acceptance of proposed credit with Nebula.
- Kimberly: prepare credit memo and DocuSign template if customer requests signature.

Ben Carter
Senior Billing Operations | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Sofia / Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear investigation summary.

We accept the provisional credit and appreciate the remediation notes. A couple of bookkeeping asks so we can close this on our side:
- Please send the credit memo (invoice_NEB-202711-Jul-credit.pdf) with VAT lines showing the negative amounts.
- Our AR team prefers a signed credit memo for EU tax reconciliation. If you can send the DocuSign link, we'll sign and confirm receipt.
- Also confirm that the one-week log export will be available at the Drive link you shared (we need the raw request_ids for our audit).

Once we receive the credit memo and sign the DocuSign, we'll proceed with the July payment (less the credited amount).

Thanks again — appreciate the responsiveness.
